minutes.headline: Conservation Commission continued the Townsend Harbor Road, warehouse and Pleasant Street hearings and cleared Sunset Lane work.
not_audible: Vote counts were read as roll calls; some names are garbled so the tally is partly unclear.
Whether the 23 Cove Road enforcement motion was a formal vote is unclear; it was settled by consensus.
Exact parcel numbers and some speaker identities are garbled.
The warehouse storage use was still being determined and was not stated.

public_comment.topic: Applicant's consultant tried to speak early on the Townsend Harbor Road tree cutting, then answered about permits, stumps, dumpster and the cut tree.
Homeowner of 23 Cove Road discussed the greenhouse and raised beds in the buffer, leaf dumping by neighbors and plans for plantings.

minutes.summary: The commission heard several wetlands hearings and continued three of them for further plans and review, while closing out two. It handled an enforcement matter, cutting plans, land-status reclassifications, certificates and tree removals. The chair and a member clashed over circulating 40B research.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission continued the 441 Townsend Harbor Road hearing, with the applicant to amend the notice of intent and provide a plan.
The commission continued the Leominster-Shirley Road warehouse hearing to September 1, with the applicant to send the Graves peer review report.
It approved the Sunset Lane work with erosion control around spoils piles, and continued the Pleasant Street hearing to September 1.
The 23 Cove Road matter stays an enforcement action, with a site visit to be arranged with the DPW superintendent.
The chair rejected a workshop on the commission's role in the 40B application research, and no resolution was reached.

why_it_matters: The warehouse and Pleasant Street subdivision hearings remain open, so neighbors and abutters have no final wetlands decision on either project yet.

The commission voted to ask town counsel about special town meeting articles on two parcels and to reclassify three parcels to the select board's care and control, which could reach residents as town meeting votes.
watch_next: September 1 continued hearings on the Leominster-Shirley Road warehouse and Pleasant Street subdivision.
October 6 continued hearing on 48 Pearl Street.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The records agree on most votes: continuances, the pool determination, the Sunset Lane conditions, the bow hunting amendment and the certificates. The main conflicts are the 48 Pearl Street continuance date (October 6 vs September 1) and the parcel ownership votes, where ours describes an assessor split and a reclassification to the select board that the official minutes do not record.
